From this machine every repository under github.com/OpenRadioss answers 404 (including OpenRadioss/OpenRadioss itself; `gh api orgs/OpenRadioss/repos` returns []). Separately, GitHub *release-asset* downloads are blocked from this box in general: a known-good asset (psf/numpy v2.4.6 tarball) also answers 404, so no extlib.zip can be fetched from any URL in any organisation. ghcr.io is not usable either (token endpoint 403, anonymous pull denied). gaps: h3dpublic_defs.h does not define H3D_NF_FORMAT (h3d_dl.c:258-281, :276-281, :1370-1417; 77 call sites in engine/source/output/h3d/h3d_build_cpp/*.cpp)
Hyper3DElementBegin/Hyper3DElement2Begin lack the H3D_ID type_id parameter (h3d_dl.c:172-179, :1192-1223 vs c_h3d_create_beams.cpp:97-99, c_h3d_create_rbe2.cpp:94-96)

version_gaps.abi_conclusion: genuinely incompatible: with the old writer the arguments after type_id shift inside the callee, and the pinned tree additionally disagrees with itself about the position of H3D_NF_FORMAT (C++ call sites 6th/7th, shim wrappers h3d_dl.c:1371-1416 last). version_gaps.enforcement: h3d output is REFUSED, not merely declared inadmissible: tools/oracle/oracle_env.sh deliberately does not export RAD_H3D_PATH, so h3d_dl.c:920-921 returns *IERROR = 1 and genh3d.F:729-731 aborts with MSGID 274 + ARRET(2). Measured: with RAD_H3D_PATH set, the tensile engine reaches NORMAL TERMINATION and writes TENSILE.h3d; without it, the same run stops with 'MESSAGE ID : 274 / ** ERROR: H3D EXTERNAL LIBRARY NOT FOUND'.
version_gaps.not_substituted: No stand-in was written for the h3d ABI. An earlier revision shipped a p0_h3d_writer_adapter.c claiming a version-gate safety net; it was dead code (h3d_dl.c:984-1000 already defines both wrappers, so the archive member was never pulled in and `strings` on both binaries found 0 references). It has been deleted, and tests/test_p0_oracle_build.py now fails if any declared adapter is not present in the binary that uses it.

extlib_shims.kind: source adapter (C), linked into the starter
extlib_shims.implemented_on: libhm_reader_linux64.so v59 primitives GlobalModelSDIGetIncludesList(char**) and GlobalModelSDICountIncludeFiles(int*), resolved by dlsym from their mangled names; reference semantics in reader/source/solver_interface/source/cfg_reading/GlobalModelSdi.cpp:2666-2693 and cpp_get_include_files_list.cpp:33-45
extlib_shims.trust_statement: the include-file list of the starter .out does NOT match a pristine oracle: measured on a Radioss-format deck with `#include "qadiags.inc"`, the v59 pair reports 0 includes (no INCLUDE FILES block at all), and an in-process check of GlobalModelSDIGetIncludesList (reviewer measurement) returns a non-NULL pointer to an EMPTY string, i.e. a count of 1 with a blank name. The adapter never invents a path (an unavailable name comes back blank, the value the caller already put there), but the block diverges from a pristine build; see admissible_parity_evidence['starter .out include-file list'] = no.

extlib_shims.kind: source adapter (C), interposes the v59 one-argument export with the pinned two-argument contract
extlib_shims.implemented_on: GlobalModelSDICountIncludeFiles(int*) (v59); reference semantics in reader/source/solver_interface/source/cfg_reading/cpp_get_number_of_include_files.cpp:31-43. This is also the one symbol where the cpp_* thunk cannot be used at all: its target takes ONE argument while the pinned source calls it with two
extlib_shims.trust_statement: fixes a real ABI mismatch: left alone, upstream's two-argument call writes the count through is_dyna (corrupting the caller's deck-flavour flag) and leaves num_includes at the 0 it was just given, so the include-file block silently disappears from every starter listing

extlib_shims.kind: source adapter (C), linked into the starter
extlib_shims.implemented_on: GlobalEntitySDICountElementsInPart(int*) (v59) plus GlobalEntitySDIGetId(int*,bool*) as a consistency check; reference semantics in reader/source/solver_interface/source/cfg_reading/GlobalModelSdi.cpp:2561-2585 and cpp_count_elements_in_part.cpp:36-49
extlib_shims.width_contract: ONE byte. The caller's flag is `logical(c_bool)`, which gfortran gives kind 1 / storage_size 1 (verified with a probe program); an earlier int-sized store overwrote the three bytes above it -- in hm_read_part.F the part id -- and every /PART came out as 0 (MSGERROR 494 + 402). Gated by test_oracle_starter_reads_a_multi_part_deck, which runs both a vendored and a synthesized multi-part deck and requires 0 ERROR(S) / 0 WARNING(S) and the correct ids and titles.
extlib_shims.trust_statement: 'does the /PART just read hold at least one element' is answered by the reader's own count of the currently-read entity, which is the contract hm_read_part.F relies on for message 178 and for the element-stack choice

extlib_shims.kind: NOT implemented - reports the reader's own error
extlib_shims.implemented_on: nothing: the v59 reader has no structured-ALE-mesh creator. The adapter sets message_value(38) = -1, the reader's own 'mesh not created' code
extlib_shims.trust_statement: any deck using /ALE/STRUCTURED_MESH fails loudly with upstream MSGERROR 3153 (s_ale_message.F90:210-215) instead of silently receiving a mesh of zeros; decks without the keyword never call it (hm_s_ale.F90:106-108)

compile-time only; the reachable libh3dwriter.so keeps the entry-point names, so the extra argument is passed and ignored. H3D output is refused at run time anyway (see extlib.version_gaps.enforcement)
/CHECKSUM_REPORT over H3D files is unavailable (no libh3dreader.so on this box); the checksum report over A-files/T01 is unaffected
declarations only; nothing is implemented. The old callee is one parameter short, so the arguments after type_id shift -- one of the three reasons h3d is inadmissible
declarations only; nothing is implemented. The pinned tree disagrees with itself about the H3D_NF_FORMAT position (call sites 6th/7th, wrappers last), which no header can repair

Node-force datasets cannot be written at all (nm -D | grep -ci node -> 0).

the h3d writer is deliberately unreachable at run time: never run an oracle job from a directory that contains libh3dwriter.so, and never set RAD_H3D_PATH, or the ABI-incompatible writer will be loaded and h3d files written silently wrong (the second and third dlopen trials of h3d_dl.c look in the cwd and in $ALTAIR_HOME/$ARCH)

cpp_is_part_with_elements_ is an adapter, not upstream code: it answers with the v59 reader's own element count for the currently-read part, which is the contract hm_read_part.F relies on for message 178 and the element-stack choice

the T01 channel is NOT a plain byte comparison: hist1.F:210-234 stamps ctime() (timer_c.c:30-40) into the T01 header unconditionally, so two runs of this oracle differ in the stamp and nowhere else. The admissible digest is the stamp-NORMALISED one -- see tools/validation_data/oracle_smoke.json -> t01.md5_definition and t01.md5_normalized (a raw md5 is t01.md5_raw and moves with the wall clock). That digest also keeps VERSIO(2) and CPUNAM from the same CH80 record, so it is bound to the build AND the architecture: see oracle_smoke.json -> environment.anchor_scope
nothing in this oracle was built from a third-party prebuilt binary; the two Docker Hub images that contain prebuilt starter/engine binaries were never installed
